# go.exe cross-compiles with `goos`, `goarch` and `cgo`, and changing them
# rebuilds. A Windows binary's default name ends in `.exe`, as `go build`
# names it, whether `goos` or `env` sets GOOS.
[!exec:go] skip

bit
stdout 'default ▶ go build -o hello\.exe '
stdout 'from-env ▶ go build -o greet\.exe '
exists hello.exe greet.exe
! exists hello greet
exec go version -m windows
stdout 'GOOS=windows'
stdout 'GOARCH=arm64'
exec go version -m linux
stdout 'GOOS=linux'
stdout 'GOARCH=amd64'
stdout 'CGO_ENABLED=0'

bit
! stdout '▶'

cp BUILD.bit.riscv BUILD.bit
bit
stdout 'linux ▶ go build'
! stdout 'windows ▶'
exec go version -m linux
stdout 'GOARCH=riscv64'

-- BUILD.bit --
windows = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/hello"
  output  = "windows"
  goos    = "windows"
  goarch  = "arm64"
}

linux = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/hello"
  output  = "linux"
  goos    = "linux"
  goarch  = "amd64"
  cgo     = false
}

default = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/hello"
  goos    = "windows"
}

from-env = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/greet"
  env     = { GOOS = "windows" }
}
-- BUILD.bit.riscv --
windows = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/hello"
  output  = "windows"
  goos    = "windows"
  goarch  = "arm64"
}

linux = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/hello"
  output  = "linux"
  goos    = "linux"
  goarch  = "riscv64"
  cgo     = false
}

default = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/hello"
  goos    = "windows"
}

from-env = go.exe {
  package = "./cmd/greet"
  env     = { GOOS = "windows" }
}
-- go.mod --
module example.com/m

go 1.22
-- cmd/hello/main.go --
package main

func main() { println("hello") }
-- cmd/greet/main.go --
package main

func main() { println("greet") }
